about: When a Sales Order stops being editable from either app. Decided 17 September 2026. Both test suites read this file.
the_rule: Approval ends editing, for everyone. An approved order is pushed to SAP and lives there from then on; changes go through the manufacturing team, who reduce or drop a line that has not been made and ship what has. The rest of the order stays open and stays with the rep who raised it.
why: This is the honest position rather than a new restriction. Sync-SapOrders.ps1 has only ever CREATED a SAP order - there is no code path in the repository or the sync that updates one - so an edit saved after approval changed the ERPNext document, showed the rep a new quantity, and left the factory building the old one. Refusing the edit is strictly better than pretending it landed.
no_seniority_exemption: The GM may trim an order while it is with them, because an escalation with no power to act is a rubber stamp. That is about deciding, not about editing an order the factory is working to: once it is approved nobody changes it, the GM included. No seniority makes an app edit reach SAP.
checked_as_stored: Every gate is re-checked against the order as STORED at the moment of the write, never against what the screen loaded. A manager can approve while a rep sits on the edit screen. There is no Server Script on this site to catch it afterwards.
escalation: Decided 26 September 2026 (the user). Rates come from SAP and nobody types them, so what is left to change is quantities, items and the delivery date - and those stop at the decision that settles the order. Within the credit limit that is the sales manager's approval (the rule above). Over the limit: the rep and the sales manager may change the order until the sales manager sends it to the GM; while it is with the GM only the GM may change it (they may trim it before approving - the user chose 'GM only'); once the GM has approved it nobody changes it - the sales manager pushes it to SAP as approved, or the GM withdraws by rejecting. A rejected order is open again: the rep is meant to fix it and send it back.
no_time_cutoff: Decided 11 October 2026 (the user). There used to be a second gate on top of the status: after 1 pm on the delivery date nobody but the GM could change an order. It is gone from both apps and from every message. The status alone decides: an order is open until the sales manager approves it or sends it to the GM, and the delivery date, past or future, has no say.
roles: rep = the rep who raised it; sales_manager = the manager whose team the rep is on; general_manager = the GM. Any other role is refused, as orderActions refuses it (credit_commitment.json).

messages.with_gm: This order is with the general manager. Only they can change it now.
messages.gm_approved: The general manager approved this order as it stands, so it can no longer be changed. The sales manager pushes it to SAP, or the general manager rejects it.

by_role.why: raised and waiting for the sales manager - open to all three
an old order waiting on its rates - still undecided, so open
the legacy PO-upload queue - still undecided, so open
rejected - open again, so the rep can fix it and send it back
escalated to the GM - the rep and the sales manager are locked out; the GM may trim it before deciding
approved by the GM and back with the sales manager to push - nobody changes it, the GM included
approved and with the factory - shut for everyone, as before
stored with stray spaces - read as the status it is

can_edit.why: the ordinary case: raised, not yet approved, owned by this rep
approved is the end of it, whatever else is true
approved and already in SAP - the case the rule exists for
a rejected order is editable again - the rep is meant to fix what was wrong with it
can_edit.note: false only because the fixture's default owner is not the acting rep; ownership is asserted separately. The po_status itself does not block it.

can_edit.why: an order with no status at all has never been approved, so it is open
a delivery date already past does not lock it - only a decision does (the 1 pm cutoff was dropped 11 Oct 2026)

lock_reason.why: an approved order names the SAP number, because that is what the manufacturing team asks for on the phone
approved but not yet pushed - no number to quote yet, so none is invented
an unapproved order is not locked at all
nor is one whose delivery date has passed - no reason mentions a time of day

can_delete.why: approval means production has it - deleting is refused from here on, and was before this rule
a submitted document is never deleted from a phone
